observations.why: The declarative 'we are adopting' enacts a collective decision stance — authority exercised through announced adoption rather than proposal or negotiation.
The comparative performance ratio frames the choice in proportionality terms — cost-benefit justification for the adoption decision.
Stating a migration timeline as fact enacts authority-ranking — a schedule declared rather than proposed, treating the decision as settled.
The summary note records a settled decision in declarative form — authority-ranking enacted through cataloguing an outcome as established fact.
Quantified performance gain restated as a summary metric — market-pricing proportionality carried as a recorded justification.
Timeline committed as a fixed date in summary form — authority-ranking enacted through scheduling as settled fact.
